entries.core_move: Apply linearity to convert scaled sums of causal time-domain signals into matching scaled sums of known one-sided Laplace transform pairs, setting up algebraic simplification in the s-domain.

Combine known one-sided Laplace transform pairs by matching each term in a time-domain sum or s-domain expression to its pair and applying linearity to form the corresponding composite transform or inverse transform.

Recognize and rewrite Laplace-domain expressions as numerator-over-denominator polynomial rational functions in s so they can be matched, combined, and prepared for partial-fraction inverse-transform work.
Construct a partial-fraction expansion for a rational function in s by factoring the denominator and assigning unknown coefficients to terms that align with known inverse Laplace transform pairs.

entries.lesson_title: Inverse Laplace Transform by Known Pairs
entries.core_move: Match each term in an algebraically prepared $X(s)$ to a known one-sided Laplace transform pair, then use linearity to recombine the corresponding time-domain components into $x(t)$.

entries.lesson_title: Interpreting Poles in Simple Transform Pairs
entries.core_move: Map each pole in a simple one-sided Laplace transform pair to the corresponding time-domain component, interpreting its s-plane location as a constant term, decay rate, or growth rate.
